Sam Navarro/Imagn Images Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Andrew and Tristan Tate, “hypermasculine” influencers and former professional kickboxers, remain jailed in Miami as their lawyer fights their possible extradition to the United Kingdom to face charges of rape and human trafficking. The British request for extradition triggers a process that will ultimately be decided by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But the Tate brothers have traveled to the United States repeatedly — including as recently as attending a UFC fight in Miami in April — without repercussions, despite pending criminal charges in Britain and Romania, and numerous civil lawsuits. The Tates have denied the charges. Joseph McBride, a defense attorney who represents the Tate brothers, told reporters outside the courthouse that an initial hearing July 20 was the first small step in fighting extradition. A lawyers-only meeting expected in several days to develop a schedule for filing written arguments, he said. U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis scheduled another hearing July 27. McBride is also fighting to stop having the Tate brothers held in solitary confinement. The brothers are being held in a 5-foot-by-12-foot cell, he said. “Solitary confinement is torture,” McBride said. “We’re working to get them out of there as soon as possible.” Because the case is being handled as an extradition rather than criminal complaint, bail is not available, McBride said. The arrests are the latest court action against the Tates, who have been the subject of numerous civil lawsuits alleging sexual violence and criminal prosecution in the United Kingdom and Romania. McBride said the arrests came days after the Tate brothers visited the Capitol to discuss political parties and upcoming elections, and after some members of Congress criticized them. “This feels political,” McBride said. “Of course they didn’t like it. No innocent man likes being taken to jail. It’s a horrible situation.” Who are the Tates? The Tates have millions of social media followers and are key figures in the “manosphere,” a collection of influencers, websites and spaces online. They promote fitness, lifestyle and get-rich-quick advice alongside a toxic blend of misogynistic and anti-feminist rhetoric while insisting they respect women. The brothers have faced numerous civil lawsuits and criminal investigations into potential sexual abuse. A civil lawsuit in Palm Beach, Florida, is proceeding and Andrew Tate faces trial in Britain this year in a civil case brought by four women who allege physical and sexual abuse from 2013 to 2015. Two of the women said they were in an intimate relationship with Tate while the two worked for his online webcam business. Tate denies the allegations and contends all sexual activity was consensual. Besides the British charges, the brothers face criminal proceedings in Romania, where authorities have been investigating them since December 2022. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier opened a criminal investigation into the Tates, characterizing its scope as “what very much appears to be soliciting, trafficking, preying upon women around the world.” What are the United Kingdom charges? The United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service announced a slew of charges against the Tates shortly before the brothers were arrested July 18 by U.S. Marshals based on an extradition warrant. The charges against Andrew Tate include seven new counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges for offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate is being prosecuted on one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. The charges are in addition to 21 original charges, including rape and human trafficking, brought in the United Kingdom, bringing the total charges against both brothers to 59. “We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the Special Crime Division at the Crown Prosecution Service, said in a statement. “These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven.” McBride issued a statement asking followers to “pray for” the brothers in their fight against “baseless” allegations. McBride, who has been defending the Tates in a civil defamation case in Palm Beach, Florida, accused the British government of seeking extradition before the civil case collapsed. “This extradition demand has one purpose: to kidnap Andrew and Tristan through paperwork before an American jury exposes the truth to the entire world,” McBride said in a statement. President Donald Trump courted members of the manosphere in his election campaign, including appearing on podcasts hosted by allies of the Tate brothers. After the Tate brothers were arrested in Romania, Donald Trump Jr. posted on social media that the prosecution was “absolute insanity.” The New York Times reported in December 2025 that the Tates had long cultivated friendships and influence with the president’s allies, including his youngest son, Barron Trump, who communicated with Andrew Tate over Zoom. But the Trump administration denied any connection to the Tates, calling the reports “fake news.” Rubio must ultimately decide whether to extradite the Tate brothers. The Justice Department traditionally examines whether the allegations merit extradition. The factors include any statutes of limitations, evidence of crimes, severity of allegations, whether the charges appear politically motivated and the nationality of the suspects. “If the court finds the fugitive to be extraditable, it certifies the extradition and sends the record to the Secretary of State, who decides whether to surrender the fugitive,” according to a Justice Department manual. Appeals are possible. The Tate brothers have dual citizenship with the United States and the United Kingdom. McBride argued that “America does not do Britain’s political dirty work.” “We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts the egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,” McBride said. https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/08/12/bux.text: Menü Kereső Történelmi rekordon a BUX, 150 ezer ponton zárt szerdán a magyar index Gazdaság Előd Fruzsina Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Újabb csúcsot ért el szerdán a magyar tőzsde, a BUX első alkalommal zárt 150 000 pont felett – derül ki a BÉT közleményéből. Az 1991-ben 1000 pontról induló index, ami a legnagyobb tőkeértékű és forgalmú hazai részvények teljesítményét követi nyomon, és a magyar tőkepiac legfontosabb mutatószámának számít, mostanra százötvenszeresére emelkedett, az indulás óta évi átlagos 15,11 százalékos évesített hozamot érve el. A 100 ezer pontot alig több mint fél évvel ezelőtt érte el a BUX. A tavaszi parlamenti választások után jelentősen meglódult több olyan vállalat részvényárfolyama, amik az index jelentős részét kiteszik, így például a Mol (ami a fél évvel ezelőttihez képest plusz 36 százalékon áll) és az OTP (ami plusz 20 százalékot szedett össze ugyanebben az időszakban). A közlemény szerint a Budapesti Értéktőzsde eredményei nemcsak az index teljesítményét, hanem a piac bővülését is jól tükrözik. 2015 óta a magyar tőzsde mérete több mint négyszeresére nőtt, közel 40 új részvénykibocsátó jelent meg, miközben a lakosság hazai részvényállománya is több mint ötszörösére emelkedett. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: A report released by the liberal think tank Cap in July argues that the National Guard failed to have an impact on crime in DC, Memphis and Los Angeles. Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters View image in fullscreen A report released by the liberal think tank Cap in July argues that the National Guard failed to have an impact on crime in DC, Memphis and Los Angeles. Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters Donald Trump Trump threatens $5bn lawsuit over liberal national guard policy report A report released by thinktank Cap argues the deployment of the national guard failed to have a measurable impact on crime, despite costing billions George Chidi Fri 21 Aug 2026 19.49 EDT First published on Fri 21 Aug 2026 17.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Center for American Progress (Cap) received a letter from Donald Trump’s lawyer threatening a $5bn lawsuit unless the liberal research organization retracts a report criticizing the effectiveness of the president’s National Guard rollout. The report released 13 July argues that the National Guard deployment in Washington DC, Memphis and Los Angeles failed to have a measurable impact on crime in these cities despite an estimated cost of $1.7bn. The report looks at the falling rate of crime in cities without a National Guard intervention and concludes that they are not statistically different from the rate of decrease in those that had the intervention, noting that violent crime began falling well before Trump took office in 2025. In response, Alejandro Brito, a personal lawyer of Trump, sent Cap a letter threatening suit if the center did not retract the research report, the New York Times reported Friday. Brito’s letter is a threat from Trump to sue the center in his personal capacity, and not on behalf of the federal government. When asked for comment, the White House replied: “Can you send us the letter?” CAP released a statement on Friday standing by its report and castigating the threat as an attack on the public’s right to speak truth to power. “Based on analysis of crime data, our report demonstrated facts about the National Guard deployments that are inconvenient to the Trump administration,” wrote Neera Tanden, Cap’s president and CEO. “This threatened lawsuit’s attack on facts and evidence is baseless. A fundamental protection of the First Amendment is to allow for the publication of facts and analysis that are contrary to the arguments and claims of any administration. A lawsuit is a transparent attempt to silence us. We will neither cower nor bend in the face of it.” Brito argues in a letter demanding the center’s retraction that “the effect on the mind of the reader and viewer of the Statements that Defendants intended to impose is that the President of the United States knowingly deceived the American people, manipulated crime statistics for political advantage, exploited public fear, abused military and executive authority for an ulterior purpose, staged a sham law enforcement operation, and then lied about its success.” Cap’s response to Trump’s legal complaint describes its claim of defamation as “absurd” and that its conclusions are statements of fact about their meticulous research. The report and commentary “on their face, concern crime statistics and causality, or actions of the federal government, not President Trump himself”, the center wrote in response to the threat letter. “In addition to being true, these statements cannot defame President Trump because they are not about him.” Washington’s leading liberal thinktank, Cap was founded in 2003 by former Clinton White House chief of staff John Podesta, who later served as the chair of Hillary Clinton’s 2016 presidential campaign. https://euobserver.com/232841/ukraine-us.text: Every day, the Ukraine Battlefield update newsletter offers a clear look at how the war is unfolding on the ground. Subscribe for free here to get the full text delivered to your inbox. A new detailed photograph and fresh information have emerged on the missions of former Slovak MiG-29s. Large Nato manoeuvres took place near Kaliningrad. A unique electronic warfare aircraft also took part. The Russians are approaching Dobropillia and will also try to encircle it. The Kupiansk sector is “close to catastrophe”, according to a Ukrainian analyst. Maps of the day — where former Slovak aircraft are also attacking Russian bridges; Kupiansk; the battle for Dobropillia. Videos of the day — an attack on a Russian bridge, of the kind also carried out by former Slovak MiG-29s; a shot-down drone fell onto an apartment block in Moscow; a whiff of the First World War in aerial warfare; a petrol station in Belgorod region wrapped in an anti-drone net. The information in this text is a summary of events on Tuesday (18 August). The situation may have changed since then. A new detailed photograph and fresh information have emerged on the missions of former Slovak MiG-29s. Last week, Ukraine’s air force lost one aircraft of this type. However, it is not known whether it was an original Ukrainian aircraft or one of those donated. On Tuesday, the Russians also said they had shot down another MiG-29 in the Donetsk region. Since Ukrainians openly report losses of their aircraft and pilots, and have so far confirmed nothing in this case, it is more likely that the Russian claims are incorrect. Of course, it cannot be ruled out that they will be confirmed later, but that is not currently the case. Even without this, Ukrainian MiG-29 losses in this war have been high. Since the start of the invasion, they have reached 38 destroyed or damaged aircraft of this type, according to the Oryx project . In addition to combat losses, wear and tear from intensive deployment must also be taken into account. Keeping decades-old combat aircraft in the air must be becoming increasingly difficult. Nevertheless, aircraft supplied by Slovakia are still fighting. In spring 2023, the Slovak army sent 13 aircraft to Ukraine. Four flew there under their own power, while the rest were probably transported by land. From time to time, a photograph appears on Ukrainian social media showing that some are still flying — a very welcome surprise given Russia’s substantial air superiority and the length of their deployment. Today, a Ukrainian pilot who uses the name Air Fighter on social media published a new image. It shows an aircraft that carried the number 3709 in Slovak air force service. The appearance of the fields below and the sentence, “Photograph from recent flights,” show that this is not an old photograph. The pilot took the photograph from the cockpit of an aircraft bearing the typical Ukrainian “pre-invasion” camouflage. It is therefore an original Ukrainian MiG-29. The second aircraft in the image came from Slovakia. In front of the cockpit, it has distinctive IFF antennas in the form of five small plates immediately behind the radar cover — a system used by Nato to identify aircraft in the air. Our former aircraft are also characterised by a black flat antenna behind the cockpit. Both types of antennas are the result of the modernisation after which our aircraft were designated MiG-29AS. However, Polish aircraft donated to Ukraine had the same equipment as well. The former Slovak aircraft 3709 can be identified by the camouflage pattern beneath the cockpit. You can find a photograph of it from 2018, when it was still in Slovak service, for example, here . Further important details can be gleaned from Air Fighter’s recent photograph. His aircraft (presumably this is a selfie) is armed with short-range air-to-air missiles, meaning that it was carrying out a fighter mission. The former Slovak 3709, however, carries pylons under its wings fitted with US GBU-39 SDB precision-guided bombs. Ukrainians therefore use this particular MiG-29 for bombing missions, such as the one in the following video. Of course, there is no evidence that the bridge shown in the footage was destroyed by an aircraft formerly operated by the Slovak army, but it is highly likely that it is among the aircraft used for the same tasks. The Ukrainian Air Force continues its summer campaign to knock out Russian bridges behind the frontline. Seen here, a Ukrainian Air Force MiG-29 Fulcrum drops a quartet of GBU-39 SDB glide bombs on the Russian bridge over the Seym River at Zvannoe. pic.twitter.com/DgJ4jT2wsj — OSINTtechnical (@Osinttechnical) August 19, 2026 OSINT analysts geolocated the previous attack in Russia’s Kursk region, close to Ukraine’s Sumy. Location (51.387555, 34.553908) https://t.co/1PHx6YgQ7Y Per local channels, the bridge was dropped on August 4th. pic.twitter.com/6zLihVLoaV — OSINTtechnical (@Osinttechnical) August 19, 2026 This is part of a wider Ukrainian air force effort to destroy Russian bridges close to the front line. The following map marks the locations where this occurred during the summer. It is almost certain that some of the crosses on it are the work of former Slovak aircraft 3709. Ukraine's summer bridge strike campaign: pic.twitter.com/nhdTUqxceO — OSINTtechnical (@Osinttechnical) August 19, 2026 Large Nato manoeuvres took place near Kaliningrad. A unique electronic warfare aircraft also took part. For almost the whole of Tuesday, numerous military analysts commented on extensive activity by Nato air forces, particularly over north-eastern Poland and the Baltic states. Around 50 military aircraft of various categories took part, operating also in the immediate vicinity of Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave. Given the location, the event naturally received intensive coverage in Poland. Defence24, a Polish military website, cited a Nato statement saying that the exercise had been planned in advance and was unrelated to Russian activity. Unofficial speculation suggested that it was prompted by Russian movements in the Baltic Sea, intelligence warnings of allegedly impending Russian provocations, and a Nato show of force intended to prevent them. Citing his sources, Polish military analyst Jaroslaw Wolski said that more than 50 aircraft took part in the operation. He noted that the exercise had not been preceded by the usual announcements and said it was the largest so far. It was also accompanied by the deployment of a Danish battalion to the Baltic states, which resembled a convoy operation escorted by warships, five Poseidon reconnaissance aircraft and Gripen fighter jets. AWACS early-warning aircraft, tanker aircraft and the latest F-35s also took part in the exercise. However, the presence of a US Air Force EA-37B drew the most attention. The United States only introduced the first aircraft of this type into service in 2024. It is designed to carry out offensive electronic operations, including the jamming of radar, communications and other electronic equipment. Source: Wikipedia — US Air Force EA-37B. The flight paths of the EA-37B, AWACS and tanker aircraft can be seen on this map from another Polish account: 📅 18.08 🕘 11:29LT - 🇺🇸✈️⛽️ Piąty tankowiec w rejonie ćwiczeń W rejon gdzie odbywają się dzisiaj duże ćwiczenia sojusznicze, doleciała właśnie kolejna latająca cysterna ✈️ Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker "60-0353" Sił Powietrznych Stanów Zjednoczonych #USAF 🇺🇸, który wystartował z… pic.twitter.com/Kqb91p30hn — Polish Military Radar 🇵🇱📡✈️ (@PolishMilRadar) August 18, 2026 Wolski saw the operation as a “clear signal to the Russians ... should anything enter Polish or Baltic airspace”. He believed Russia had first received a political message that Nato was aware of the planned provocations, and that the exercise was a deterrent display of strength. “An exercise of this scale was not announced in advance, so what we are seeing is a sudden deployment of the so-called Allied support forces to the area of operations,” Wolski wrote, echoing other analysts in Poland. The Kupiansk sector is “close to catastrophe”, according to a Ukrainian analyst. “The Kupiansk sector is one of those areas that does not receive enough attention. The left bank of the Oskil is hell on earth,” Bohdan Myroshnykov wrote . He considered the situation near Kupiansk comparable to, if not worse than, that in Kostiantynivka. The Russians even claimed to have again penetrated Kupiansk itself, but Ukrainian sources did not confirm this. The fact remains, however, that units south-east of the city, on the eastern bank of the Oskil river, are in a critical position: under constant bombardment and with the river behind them, greatly complicating movement and logistics. “Withdrawing from positions is a special operation in itself, and it is far from always successful,” Myroshnykov said. “The situation in this sector can be described as close to catastrophic,” he said, adding that there was little point in drawing maps here, as all of them were merely indicative. Petrenko acknowledged the presence of Russians in Kupiansk’s left-bank suburbs, in the villages of Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi and Kivsharivka: This is consistent with the map by the Finnish OSINT project Black Bird Group . More for amusement than information, we are also including a map by the Russian state agency Ria Novosti, according to which Kupiansk has been captured and the Ukrainian bridgehead on the Oskil no longer exists. The Russians are approaching Dobropillia and will also try to encircle it. Most recently, the aggressor’s soldiers reached the village of Krasnopillia, less than three km from the city’s southern boundary. Their presence was recorded by the Ukrainian Telegram channel Petrenko, whose map is below. It is not yet known whether this was a “flag operation” or whether the Russians managed to hold the village. A Russian Telegram channel also recorded an advance in Krasnopillia. Its map, however, is traditionally considerably more dramatic than Ukrainian and independent ones. Videos of the day Even the simplest solutions can work. It is well known that Ukrainians also use old Yak-52 training aircraft to repel drone attacks. The following compilation shows how they do it. This method of fighting is a return to the beginning of the First World War. Military aircraft were still primitive at the time, and the first aerial duels took place in exactly this way: aviators fired rifles at each other from unarmed aircraft. In 2026, shotguns have replaced them, but the principle is the same. 🤯 WOW: A Ukrainian Yak-52 backseat gunner shoots down Russian Shahed attack drones with a rifle. pic.twitter.com/GdAJtqXJTv — UNITED24 Media (@United24media) August 18, 2026 Tuesday saw the largest attack on Moscow since the start of the war. It is generally considered to have been unsuccessful. However, images of a damaged apartment block in the Russian capital circulated online. Footage from a nearby building shows that a shot-down Ukrainian drone fell onto the damaged building. Moscovites are delighted pic.twitter.com/RZ1mzBvPLC — Kvist (@kvistp) August 18, 2026 A Russian petrol station in Belgorod region is literally wrapped in an anti-drone net. 🇷🇺 #Russia #Belgorod border region pic.twitter.com/h782RSwhSM — C4H10FO2P ☠️ (@markito0171) August 18, 2026 What are the losses No change on Tuesday morning. By Monday (17 August), Russia had verifiably lost 24,005 pieces of heavy equipment (23,982 on Monday, 10 August). Of these, Ukrainians destroyed 18,977 (18,957), 997 (995) were damaged, crews abandoned 1,193 (1,193), and the Ukrainian army captured 2,838 (2,837). This includes 4,437 (4,437) tanks, of which 3,343 (3,343) were destroyed in combat. Ukraine lost 11,916 (11,828) pieces of equipment, of which 9,333 (9,286) were destroyed, 695 (695) damaged, 692 (691) abandoned, and 1,196 (1,196) captured. This includes 1,450 (1,450) tanks, of which 1,111 (1,111) were destroyed in combat. Note: Neither side regularly reports its own deaths or destroyed equipment. Ukraine publishes daily figures for Russian casualties and destroyed equipment, but these cannot be independently verified. This overview uses data from the Oryx project , which has compiled a list of equipment losses documented exclusively by photographs since the start of the war. Unlock article and share MiG-29AS, formerly in service with the Slovak Air Force, during a mission over Ukraine. Photo: Telegram, Air Fighter. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: A town hall in the French city of Limoges was set on fire during the protests. Photograph: SDIS 87/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A town hall in the French city of Limoges was set on fire during the protests. Photograph: SDIS 87/AFP/Getty Images France France hit by debt sell-off as protests unnerve investors Difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs widens after violence breaks out Business live – latest updates Lauren Almeida Mon 19 Oct 2026 03.32 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 07.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google France has been hit by a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets after violent protests over the weekend left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops looted and thousands of arrests across the country. Almost 2,400 people have been arrested in France, the interior ministry said on Sunday, with police deploying teargas in confrontations with protesters . The French president, Emmanuel Macron, condemned the “unbridled violence” in a televised address on Sunday night. “Looking at these images, we all asked ourselves: what is going through their minds? How can French people do this to France ?” he said. The chaos has spooked investors in France’s government debt, with the yield on its 10-year yield rising by 10 basis points to 4.89% on Monday. Yields rise when prices fall. This widened the difference between the French and German 10-year borrowing costs – which is a metric for the risk premium attached to French debt. Meanwhile, the two-year yield rose by five basis points to 3.6%. Concerns about France’s instability knocked the euro down to a 17-month low against the pound on Monday morning, with sterling rising to €1.188. Violence erupted across France after weeks of peaceful demonstrations over conditions in schools and the cost of living. While tens of thousands of people have attended peaceful marches to demand more teachers and repairs to decrepit schools, different groups have clashed with police in cities including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille. Jim Reid of Deutsche Bank said the protests “won’t make it easy for the international community to be totally comfortable buying OATs [French government bonds]”. He said: “With France already facing a difficult fiscal backdrop and the 2027 election approaching, the weekend adds another layer of political risk for markets.” The 30-year bond, which is a benchmark for the French government’s long-term cost of borrowing, rose by five basis points to 5.42%. The rise in borrowing costs will add further strain to France’s public finances, as the government also tries to pass a budget for next year to rein in its deficit . skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion France’s debt-to-GDP stood at 115.6% in 2025, while its budget deficit was 5.1%, compared with 94.3% and 4.3% for the UK respectively. The unrest adds to “concerns about the political and fiscal troubles in France”, said Neil Wilson, Saxo UK’s investor strategist. “It underscores how hard it will be for a government to enact the kind of spending restraint required to get the deficit down.” The French government is preparing a budget that would involve cutting pensions spending and funding for government departments, excluding defence. However, there are growing fears that political pressure could derail these plans, which could push up borrowing and add more to the country’s debt pile. The euro also slipped against the US dollar, down by 0.4% in early trading on Monday, falling to $1.1197. The French Cac 40, which tracks the biggest companies listed in Paris, fell by 1.2% in morning trading, compared with a 0.7% drop on the pan-European Stoxx Europe 600 index. French bank stocks were among the fallers, with Société Générale and BNP Paribas down more than 2%.
